findings.source_quote: ἡ γὰρ ἐνθύμησις αὕτη Θεοῦ δούλῳ ἁμαρτία μεγάλη ἐστίν
findings.issue: The theological decision records “slave of God,” and the lexical decision likewise records “slave,” although the reader text correctly uses “servant of God.” Their rationales also incorrectly claim that current project policy favors “slave” when belonging to God is salient. Current policy requires reader-facing “servant,” with bonded-status nuance preserved in notes or audit metadata. This is a contradictory decision record and a false policy attribution, not a defect in the reader-facing “servant.”
findings.suggested_revision: Update both decision records to identify “servant” as the actual chosen rendering. Correct their policy rationales to explain that bonded status, belonging, and obligation may be documented without replacing reader-facing “servant.” Preserve superseded decisions as explicitly historical records rather than presenting them as current choices. Review the revised metadata before acceptance.

findings.source_quote: ἡ γὰρ ἐνθύμησις αὕτη Θεοῦ δούλῳ ἁμαρτία μεγάλη ἐστίν
findings.issue: Independently checked against the Greek, the simplified reader text correctly says “servant of God.” Its theological and lexical metadata nevertheless record “slave” as the chosen rendering and incorrectly attribute that choice to current project policy. The supplied simplified edition therefore contains the same concrete decision-record contradiction, even though its reader-facing terminology is compliant.
findings.suggested_revision: Record “servant” as the current choice in both metadata blocks and replace the inaccurate policy attribution with the current servant policy. Retain any historically salient bonded-status explanation as nuance, not as a conflicting main-text choice. Label retained earlier decisions as historical and submit the corrected metadata for fresh review.

summary: Both reader texts were independently reviewed against all eleven source paragraphs. No concrete reader-text fidelity defect was identified: the conditional sequence, thought/deed distinction, death assertion, required reception, repentance limitation, remarriage prohibition, reciprocal application, and healing ability remain intact. Editorial brackets are disclosed, and the stated frequency/duration and image-making/imitation alternatives are preserved without displacing the disclosed working readings. The witness notes are compatible with the supplied attributed reports; this does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation. Both editions require minor revision because their current servant metadata contradicts their reader text and misstates project policy.
